skills.strategy: Apply ARRAY_PARTITION (cyclic or complete) so local arrays expose enough read/write ports for the unroll factor. Complete partition for small partial-sum arrays; cyclic factor=UF for lane buffers.

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW structure passes csynth but latency is high because compute tasks lack ARRAY_PARTITION, inner UNROLL, and parallel load/store overlap
skills.strategy: After correct DATAFLOW task boundaries, maximize throughput: partition local arrays on the inner compute dimension, UNROLL inner loops to match partition factor, pipeline innermost loops II=1, run independent load tasks in parallel on distinct gmemN bundles, and use hls::stream depth 4–16 for tile pipelines to overlap load(t+1) with compute(t).

add #pragma HLS UNROLL factor=UF on innermost reduction/dot-product loop
pipeline innermost memory/compute loop with II=1; never outer row loop PIPELINE for multi-matrix loads
issue parallel load tasks only when each touches a different m_axi port/bundle
for tiled kernels use hls::stream tile FIFO between load_tile, compute_tile, store_tile for real overlap
target higher DSP/FF utilization when latency slack exists — prefer parallelism over minimal resources
guards: partition/unroll must not break DATAFLOW buffer ownership rules

skills.strategy: Use UF private partial accumulators with complete partition; unrolled init; pipelined fixed-bound loop with unrolled lane updates and guards; final reduction of partial[] into result scalar.

unrolled init of partial[p] = 0
outer pipelined loop steps by UF over fixed TILE_SIZE bound
inner unrolled lane updates partial[p] with guarded index
after loop, sum partial[] into output scalar or local
guards: only use when lane iterations are independent
match UF to unroll factor and memory ports

skills.pattern: static-bound GEMM/matmul-like OR triangular syrk/syr2k/symm nests on local buffers (C[i][j] += ... over k, or C[i][j] += A[j][k]*B[i][k]+... with if (j<=i)) where PIPELINE II=1 is placed only on an inner j (L4) under sequential outer i (L1) and/or sequential k (L3), so csynth shows L1 trip=M Pipelined=no and latency ≈ M*(K*N+Depth) instead of one flattened (i,j) pipeline
skills.strategy: Partition locals on the reduction dim k; PIPELINE II=1 the (i,j) nest with k fully unrolled; LOOP_FLATTEN (or single ij loop). For syrk/syr2k: keep FIXED j<N bounds with if (j<=i) guards (never for (j=0;j<=i)); optionally separate beta-scale pass, then one update pass that reduces over k inside each (i,j) iteration. Reject L1 sequential + only L4 II=1. Success also requires achieved Final II near 1 (or best legal). Full k UNROLL with a serial FP accumulator is insufficient if II stays huge — use partial/tree sums or enough FP operators, else pipeline-on-k (hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll).
required_steps: confirm M,N,K (or N,M for syr2k) are compile-time constants and compute is on local arrays
ARRAY_PARTITION A/B (and C as needed) on the k-accessed dimension — complete if budget allows
rewrite triangular loops to fixed bound + if (j<=i) / if (j<i) guards — never variable trip j<=i as loop bound
prefer two phases for syr2k/syrk: (1) scale C*=beta on triangle with PIPELINE+FLATTEN; (2) update with (i,j) PIPELINE+FLATTEN and k fully UNROLL
place PIPELINE II=1 on the (i,j) nest with fully unrolled k; add LOOP_FLATTEN or collapse to ij
success check: csynth must NOT show L1/compute_outer trip=M Pipelined=no next to only an L4 II=1; prefer one flattened trip ≈ M*N
re-check device Utilization (%) ≤ 100; if complete on k overshoots, use cyclic factor matched to unroll
after flatten+k-unroll, check Final II; if II ≫ 1 from serial FP acc / shared dmul/dadd, apply hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll
guards: do not apply this flatten mandate to true outer tile loops over partial tiles — only full-workspace or within-tile (i,j) nests with static bounds
preserve numerical semantics of reductions
resource legality: BRAM/DSP/FF/LUT/URAM device util ≤ 100%
full k UNROLL requires a parallel reduction structure or enough FP units — a single serial float/double accumulator alone is not success if Final II ≫ 1
do not complete-partition an entire large buffer when only one dimension is accessed in parallel — partition that dimension
do not refuse complete/cyclic on the reduction (k) dimension of a static-bound GEMM when k is fully unrolled under PIPELINE II=1; that banking is required for nest flatten
do not partition dimensions not accessed in parallel
avoid partitioning when the bottleneck is off-chip memory bandwidth
if complete on the parallel dim blows FF/BRAM, fall back to cyclic factor matched to unroll and keep flatten
skills.pattern: a local array needs more read/write ports for pipelined or unrolled access, but the correct partition style depends on access pattern and array size
required_steps: identify the parallel access pattern
identify the accessed array dimension (for GEMM C[i][j]+=A[i][k]*B[k][j], that is dim k of A and B)
choose complete/cyclic/block based on size and indexing; for fully unrolled k, prefer complete on k if budget allows else cyclic matched to unroll
match factor to unroll factor or port demand
check II, nest flatten (outer trip must not remain sequential), and resource usage
skills.strategy: choose complete partition for small arrays or for a parallel access dimension that must supply many ports in one cycle (including GEMM reduction dim k when fully unrolled), cyclic partition for regular interleaved lane accesses, and block partition for contiguous per-worker regions. Prefer cyclic/block when factor << size; allow complete on the parallel dim when size is modest (about <=64-128) OR when II=1 flatten of a static GEMM nest requires it.

skills.pattern: syr2k/syrk/symm-style nest on locals: L1 over i sequential; optional L2 beta scale; L3 over k; L4 over j with PIPELINE II=1 and if (j<=i) — csynth L1 trip=N Pipelined=no, iteration latency ≈ L2 + L3_L4 (e.g. ~4934), total ≈ N*that (e.g. ~394k for N=80)
skills.strategy: Do not pipeline only L4 under sequential L1/L3. Use FIXED j<N (and i<N, k<M) bounds with if (j<=i) guards. Separate beta scale (PIPELINE+LOOP_FLATTEN on (i,j)). Then one update pass: PIPELINE+LOOP_FLATTEN on (i,j), fully UNROLL k, ARRAY_PARTITION A/B on k dim so each (i,j) iteration does the full reduction in one II. Optional fuse: C = beta*C + alpha*sum in one pass. Never use for (j=0; j<=i; ++j) as the loop bound.
required_steps: stage A,B,C into locals if not already (load/store keep PIPELINE II=1, fixed bounds)
ARRAY_PARTITION local_A and local_B complete (or cyclic) on the k dimension (dim=2 for [N][M])
rewrite any j<=i / k<i loop bounds to fixed N/M + if guards
phase scale: for i, for j < N { PIPELINE II=1; LOOP_FLATTEN; if (j<=i) C[i][j]*=beta; }
phase update: for i, for j < N { PIPELINE II=1; LOOP_FLATTEN; if (j<=i) { sum=0; for k UNROLL sum+=...; C[i][j]+=alpha*sum; } }
success: top latency much below N*(M*N); L1 must not remain Pipelined=no with iter latency ≈ M*N
keep BRAM/DSP/FF/LUT/URAM device util ≤ 100%

pipeline the surrounding loop when appropriate

validate correctness

guards: do not complete-partition an entire large buffer blindly — partition the parallel dimension

create partial accumulators indexed by lane

pipeline the main loop and unroll the lane loop
perform final reduction across partial accumulators
check numerical tolerance for floating-point or non-associative expressions
skills.strategy: replace the single accumulator with lane-local partial accumulators, update them in parallel, and combine them with a final tree or cleanup reduction; preserve serial order only when exact order is required

guards: do not privatize state that intentionally coordinates lanes or enforces order

determine whether the state can be made independent per lane or per work item
reshape state as state[LANES][...] or state[PE][...]
partition the lane/PE dimension completely
rewrite each lane to access only its own state
merge or copy back final state only if semantically required
skills.strategy: make state lane-local or PE-local, partition the state dimension completely, and merge or reconcile state after the parallel section when needed

guards: do not use this when the exact sequential update order is semantically required

skills.pattern: a pipelined loop performs read-modify-write updates to an array element, such as hist[key] += v, acc[idx] = acc[idx] + v, or scatter accumulation, and the scheduler cannot prove that consecutive iterations update different addresses

determine whether collisions can occur across iterations and whether accumulation is associative enough for partial merging
create lane-local, PE-local, bank-local, or tile-local copies of the accumulator
partition the privatized dimension completely so each lane has independent storage ports
rewrite the hot loop to update only its private accumulator copy
add a separate merge loop or tree reduction over private copies
pipeline the hot update loop and the merge loop where legal
validate numerical equivalence, especially for floating-point accumulation order
skills.strategy: privatize the accumulator array by lane, processing element, bank, or tile; perform independent read-modify-write updates locally; then merge the partial arrays in a separate reduction/merge phase so the hot update loop can pipeline without same-array inter-iteration hazards

guards: only scalarize when no other code observes the intermediate array updates during the loop

skills.pattern: a loop repeatedly reads and writes the same scalar-like array element or a small fixed set of array elements, creating an avoidable memory read-after-write dependence through an array port

write the final scalar/register state back after the loop or tile
pipeline the hot loop and inspect whether the memory dependence disappears
skills.strategy: scalarize the hot read-modify-write state into registers, update the scalar inside the pipelined loop, and write the array element back once after the loop or after the tile; for a small fixed set, completely partition the state and keep each element in a separate register

guards: do not unroll memory-bound AXI load loops expecting high unroll to help — widen/burst or stage first
do not unroll across true loop-carried dependencies

skills.pattern: a loop has independent iterations or a safely transformable reduction, and latency is dominated by arithmetic throughput rather than global-memory bandwidth
required_steps: identify independent loop iterations or a safely transformable reduction
if the trip count is a small compile-time constant (typical PolyBench/ChatHLS mini: <=64, often 30-42), use complete `#pragma HLS UNROLL` — do NOT default to factor=2 or factor=4
only use partial `#pragma HLS UNROLL factor=N` when complete unroll would clearly exceed device budget or the trip count is large/variable
partition or bank local arrays to MATCH the unroll (complete partition for complete unroll; cyclic factor=N for partial) — never mismatch (e.g. partition factor=4 with unroll factor=2)
avoid increasing parallelism beyond available on-chip memory ports / AXI bandwidth for load loops

validate csim/cosim and compare achieved latency
skills.strategy: For small static nests (atax/bicg/mvt/gesummv-sized), prefer complete unroll of the independent inner dimension with matching complete/cyclic partition. Reserve partial/conservative factors for large trip counts or proven resource pressure. Match array partitioning to the unroll factor exactly.
